newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota farmers wait for fields to dry.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota farmers wait for fields to dry.

text.p: South Dakota farmers waited for warmer weather to dry snow-covered fields and allow spring planting, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its first weekly report of the year.
"Except for isolated areas, producers across the state believe it will be a week and a half before fieldwork can begin in earnest," the report said.
One day was rated suitable for fieldwork in the week ended Sunday. Topsoil moisture as of Friday was rated nil very short, two percent short, 34 percent adequate and 64 percent surplus.

Winter wheat conditions were rated four percent very poor, 13 percent poor, 27 percent fair, 50 percent good and six percent excellent. Statewide, 60 percent of the winter wheat acreage had broken dormancy.
Spring wheat was one percent seeded, down from the five-year average of 10 percent. Oats were one percent planted. No five-year average was available.
"Producers in some areas have started planting spring wheat and oats although fieldwork generally has not started statewide," the report said.
